newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska corn develops rapidly amid humid weather.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska corn develops rapidly amid humid weather.

text.p: The Nebraska corn crop developed rapidly last week due to the humid and hot weather, but dryland corn was stressed by drying soil conditions, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Irrigated corn was 80 percent good to excellent as of Sunday, while dryland corn was 66 percent good to excellent.
Twenty-seven percent of the crop had silked, behind the 32 percent a year ago and the 33 percent average pace. Only two percent of the crop had silked as of a week ago.
Soybean conditions were three percent poor, 22 percent fair, 60 percent good and 15 percent excellent. Blooming reached 52 percent, ahead of last year's 33 percent and the 37 percent average.
Wheat harvest was 64 percent complete as of Sunday, ahead of 48 percent a year ago and the average of 52 percent.
Pasture and range conditions were four percent very poor, 17 percent poor, 35 percent fair, 38 percent good and seven percent excellent.
